div.head: VIII Atr 24
div.ab: And gif he sý mægleas, ladige mid geferan oððe fæste to corsnǽde, ⁊ þaræt gefare þæt þæt God ræde.
And gif he sý mægleas, ladige mid geferan, oððe fæste to corsnǽde ⁊ þaræt gefare þæt þæt God ræde.
And gif he sy mægleas, ladige mid geferan oððe fæste to corsnæde, and þaræt gefare þæt þæt God ræde.
Und wenn er ohne Sippe ist, schwöre er sich mit [Standes]genossen rein oder faste zum [Ordal des] Entscheidungsbissens und erlebe dabei das, was Gott bestimmen mag.
And if he is without kin, let him clear himself with his fellows [of his order] or fast for the [ordeal of the] consecrated morsel, and experience there what God may decree.
And if he has no kin, he shall clear himself with the help of his fellow-ecclesiastics, or fast in preparation for the ordeal of consecrated bread, and experience there what God shall decree.
And if he is without kinsmen, he is to clear himself with his associates, or fast before the ordeal of the consecrated morsel, and experience at it what God decrees.
And if he is without family, he shall exonerate himself with the help of other clergy, or fast to prepare for the ordeal of consecrated bread, and there endure whatever God decides.

note.seg: So Frühere: ‘fellows in orders’ Kemble II 259; aber vielleicht enger ‘Stiftsbrüder, Mitglieder der Kleriker-Gilde’; s. o. 19
Thus earlier scholars: ‘fellows in orders’ Kemble II 259; but perhaps more narrowly ‘fellow canons, members of the clerical gild’; see above 19
Geweihter Bissen ist jedenfalls zulässig. Die Wahl trifft, laut o. 22⁴, vermutlich Richter oder Gegenpartei, nicht Beweisführer.—Man kann, laut 22, auch þar æt trennen

The consecrated morsel is in any case admissible. According to above 22⁴, the choice is presumably made by the judge or the opposing party, not by the party offering proof.—According to 22, one may also separate þar æt
